label: ercot published-ORDC curve (NP6-576-ER, grounded)
definition: PROBE. run143 keeper recipe with ONE change: the energy+reserve co-opt ORDC reserve demand curve uses ERCOT's PUBLISHED NP6-576-ER seasonal mu/sigma (ercot_ordc_lolp_params.csv, mu~924/sigma~1348) instead of the ungrounded neutral mu=0/sigma=1400 fallback. Grounded input (ERCOT's published rule), NOT fitted to the LMP. Motivation: run143's monthly shape is bimodal and the price duration curve is hollow in the P90-P99 'moderately scarce' band; the keeper curve only priced reserve ~920 MW too low. Scores (demand-wtd avg / h>200 / h>500, vs actual): 2023 45.3/156/94 (run143 36.5/104/56; actual 48.4/181/104); 2024 25.2/34/21 (run143 23.2/22/16; actual 26.8/53/16); 2025 31.5/4/1 (run143 31.4/1/0; actual 32.5/31/3). FINDING: a single grounded curve moves all 3 years' average AND scarcity-hour frequency toward actual without over-inflating 2025 or exploding (unlike the ECRS-requirement and unit-commitment probes, which both over-fired). RESIDUAL: the duration curve P90-P99 band is still under-priced (2024 model P95 27.9 vs actual 61.4), pointing the next GROUNDED structural lever at the reserve-SUPPLY definition (online/RTOLCAP vs all dispatchable headroom), not the curve. Volume re-gate pending before keeper (operating-shape gate flagged 19 regressions).
